svg.title: MPx Sub-Function to Technology Map
svg.desc: Every sub-function of the MPx process function structure mapped to candidate technologies, product methods, and interventions, grouped by main water flow and the microplastic detection branch, colour-coded by input, process, and output stage.
svg.text: MPx — CED Module 8 morphological chart (generation stage): candidate options for every sub-function, nothing selected yet
Filtration options (Step 03) are drawn from MPx_Filter_Mechanism_Map.svg; detection options (Step 08) from MPx_Detection_Methods_Comparison.docx. The rest (source ID,
water input, purification, storage, dispensing, sample collection, display) are freshly researched this round — see the sources list at the end.
left = sub-function · right = options for it (not solutions selected)
Sense / confirm source type (tap, bottle, jug,
• Manual user selection — physical mode switch or app menu
• Conductivity / TDS probe to auto-classify source quality
• No dedicated sensor — universal source-agnostic inlet
Present selectable source options to the user
• Physical rotary or slide selector on the housing
Verify source is compatible with the device
• Inlet screen / strainer as a size gate (excludes debris, insects)
• Pre-fill turbidity check, visual or optical, before accepting
• User acknowledgement / warning prompt (procedural, no sensor)
• Firmware profile switch — adjusts pump speed / detection sensitivity per source
• Simple lookup table triggered by the user’s source selection
• No adaptive signalling — fixed universal operating profile
Convey water from the source into the device
• Gravity pour-in through an open funnel / hopper
• Straw / suction draw (syringe or vacuum primer)
• Direct tap or bottle quick-connect fitting
Connect / seal the input interface to the
• Universal funnel mouth — pour-in only, no seal needed
• Passive overflow standpipe as a volume cap
• Vent hole with a hydrophobic membrane (blocks water, passes air)
• Graduated sight window / markings on the housing (passive, zero power)
• In-line paddle-wheel or turbine flow sensor
• Load-cell / weight sensing at the base
• Capacitive or float fill-level sensor (see Step 05 options)
• Air-gap inlet design — physical separation, no valve needed
options drawn directly from MPx_Filter_Mechanism_Map.svg (4 families, 24 mechanisms)
Convey water through the filter stage
Separate microplastic particles by size or
• Bio-adsorbent media — mycelium mat, nanocellulose/chitosan sponge
Regulate flow rate through the filter media
• Fixed flow-restrictor orifice downstream of the filter
Retain / trap separated particles within the
• Inherent to the chosen fine-filter mechanism above
• Backing support mesh + edge O-ring seal, prevents media bypass
• Differential-pressure sensor / switch across the filter
• Flow-rate drop-off timer (compares fill time to a baseline)
• Manual replacement-schedule reminder via app or calendar, no sensor
UV treatment stage — dose benchmarks per NSF/ANSI and UV-C LED literature
Convey filtered water to the purification
• Shared pump line from the filtration stage
Expose water to a disinfection agent or energy
• UV-C LED array, ~265 nm — NSF Class A target ≥40 mJ/cm², Class B ≥16 mJ/cm²
• Traditional UV mercury lamp — higher output but larger, fragile, being phased out
• Electrochemical disinfection — in-situ chlorine generation via electrolysis
• Fixed-residence-time flow-through tube — dose set by geometry
• Timed batch-hold cycle — valve closes, UV runs for a set duration
• Flow-rate-linked LED intensity control — dose as a function of flow speed
• UV sensor / photodiode feedback confirming LED output
• Residual chlorine test strip, for the chemical-dosing route
Neutralize or vent treatment by-products, if
• Not applicable for UV-C — no chemical by-product, a key advantage over chlorination
• Activated-carbon polishing stage for the chlorine/ozone routes
• Off-gas vent for the ozone route
• Continued pump-through into a sealed tank
Contain / hold the treated water volume
• Collapsible food-grade silicone bladder — compact / portable
• Self-sealing valve cap — opens only under suction or pressure
• Hydrostatic pressure sensor — cheapest, most power-efficient, best portable fit
• Ultrasonic level sensor — non-contact, but 10–100× more power draw
• Sight-glass / graduated window — zero power, passive
Preserve water quality over the storage period
• UV-C LED periodic recirculation / idle-state disinfection pulse
• Opaque housing — blocks light, limits algae growth
• UI reminder encouraging short storage duration (procedural)
Convey water from storage to the outlet
• Same pump line reused for dispensing
• Portion-metered pump cycle — fixed volume per press
• Silicone one-way duckbill valve at the mouthpiece, prevents backwash
• Flip-cap dust cover over the spout
Stop / shut off flow after dispensing
DETECTION BRANCH — parallel path off Step 03 (Filter Microplastics)
Branch / divert a sample stream from the main
• T-junction bleed line with a micro-valve
• Bypass loop timed to open periodically
Convey the sample to the detection zone
• Small-bore capillary tube, gravity- or pump-fed
• Dedicated micro-pump on the sample line
• Manual pipette transfer — lab-adjacent, less automated
• Secondary fine mesh / membrane trap sized to the sample volume
Hold sample volume steady for measurement
• Continuous-flow tube — inline reading, no hold
• Fluorescent tagging (Nile Red) to optically distinguish plastics from organics
• Polymer-specific spectral signature (Raman / FTIR) to exclude non-plastic hits
DETECTION / COUNT MICROPLASTICS PER UNIT VOLUME
options drawn directly from MPx_Detection_Methods_Comparison.docx (15-method Tier A/B table)
Sense presence of particles in the sample
• Smartphone camera + fluorescence excitation, Nile Red staining
• Turbidity / optical-density proxy sensor — cheap, but not MP-specific
• YOLOv5 / YOLOv8 ML classification on captured images
• Polymer-specific Raman / FTIR signature — lab-grade, likely too costly/bulky for portable
Measure particle size and / or count
• Image-processing pixel-to-size calibration, works with any camera-based method
• Manual visual count under magnification — low-cost fallback
Convert the sensed signal into quantifiable
• On-device microcontroller image processing — edge ML (TinyML-class chip)
• Cloud / phone-app processing — offloads compute, avoids FLOro’s cost overrun
• Simple threshold-comparator circuit, turbidity route only
Normalize count to a per-unit-volume value
• Firmware calculation using the known sample-chamber volume (Step 07)
• Flow-rate-linked continuous count — particles/second × known flow rate
Compare measured value against a safety
• On-device firmware threshold logic, simple pass/fail
• App-side comparison against the team’s 90% / 99% removal-efficiency target
• On-device flash memory log, timestamped readings
• Companion-app cloud or local history log
• Wired connection from the detection PCB to the display module
• BLE / Wi-Fi link to a companion phone app
• Direct analog signal to a simple indicator, no digital data
• Phone-app UI does all rendering, device just transmits raw data
Present result to the user (visual / audio /
• E-paper / e-ink screen — near-0 static power, sunlight-readable, best for infrequent updates
• Memory LCD (MIP) — 1–5 µW static, supports scrolling/animation, weeks–months battery life
• PMOLED — higher power, best contrast/speed, poor sunlight readability
• Simple RGB LED indicator array — lowest cost/power, coarse info only
• Buzzer / audio alert — fits the 30% of quiz respondents who want no visible detail
Allow switching between simple and detailed
• Long-press gesture on a single button
Indicate alert status if a threshold is
• Push notification via the companion app
This is the generation half of Module 8 — formulate the sub-function, then list independent options, as in the team’s own Detection Ranking + Morphological Matrix and
10-Concepts docs. Next: draw a small number of hand-picked paths through this map (one option per row, combined into a coherent concept), then score them against the
Weighted Objective Tree. Rows with many options (Step 03 fine-filter, Step 08 sensing/distinguishing, Step 09 display) are where the concept space actually branches, and
are most worth a team brainstorm before narrowing.
